A checklist for pet carriers in detail
A settled phase is easier when you know what to expect

Pet carrier checklist for smooth companion travel

When you are getting ready to fly with a pet, the carrier is one of the first things to check. At Aurelia Skyways, we want the trip to feel calm and predictable, so a good carrier setup makes a real difference for you and your animal.

Start with a carrier that is sturdy, secure, and easy to close. It should let your pet sit, lie down, and turn around without feeling crammed. Soft-sided or hard-sided options can both work, as long as they stay intact and do not collapse in a way that would unsettle your pet. Make sure the door or zipper closes fully and that all fasteners are in good shape.

Next, look at the inside. A clean lining or absorbent pad helps keep things comfortable if there is any spill or accident along the way. Keep loose items to a minimum, since clutter can shift and bother a nervous animal. If your pet is used to a familiar blanket or toy, bring only what fits safely and will not block airflow.

Ventilation matters, too. Good airflow helps the carrier stay comfortable during check-in and boarding. You should also check that the carrier has your contact details attached in a clear way, along with any travel documents your trip calls for. If you are unsure about what belongs with the carrier, our Companion Animal Travel Desk can walk you through the practical steps before you arrive.

Damage and readiness checks are part of the normal review. <<FACT F102>> A carrier with broken latches, rough edges, or weak seams may need attention before travel. We prefer to catch those issues early so the trip is easier for everyone, including the animal.

If your pet is anxious, keep your own movements calm when opening or closing the carrier. Gentle handling helps keep the experience settled, and it gives our team a better chance to work smoothly around the animal. We use humane methods and steady routines to support safe travel from the start.

For more help with carrier requirements, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk before your departure.
